title: Thai Basil Ground Beef Skillet
seoTitle: Thai Basil Ground Beef Skillet | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Garlic-chili ground beef simmered with green beans and basil over jasmine rice
subtitle: Garlic-chili ground beef simmered with green beans and basil over jasmine rice
description: Ground beef browns hard with garlic and chilies, then simmers with green beans in a savory-sweet fish sauce mixture until the sauce reduces and clings, finished with a big handful of basil folded in off heat.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear. Cook with a pinch of salt per package directions; fluff and hold covered while the skillet comes together.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.instruction: Stir together fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, and beef broth in a bowl so it's ready to pour in one motion.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add beef in a flat layer, let it sear undisturbed 2 minutes before breaking apart, cooking 6–7 minutes until deeply browned with no pink.

steps.title: Add aromatics and green beans
steps.instruction: Push beef to one side, add garlic, chilies, and shallots to the cleared space; cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add green beans, stir everything together, cook 2–3 minutes until beans start to soften.

steps.title: Simmer until saucy
steps.instruction: Pour in the sauce mixture, bring to a simmer, and cook 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are tender and the sauce has reduced and clings to the beef instead of pooling. This stage is forgiving — it can hold at a low simmer a few extra minutes if needed.

steps.title: Finish with basil
steps.instruction: Kill the heat, fold in basil until just wilted — overcooked basil turns bitter and black.

proTips: Reduce chilies to 2 for a milder version—offer sriracha at the line for heat seekers.
A fried egg with a runny yolk on top makes this feel like a proper Thai street-food plate.
This skillet can hold on low heat, covered, for up to 15 extra minutes if a call comes in—the sauce just reduces further, no harm done.
tonightSpread: Cucumber slices with a squeeze of lime.
leftovers: Reheats well in a skillet or microwave—the sauce keeps the beef from drying out the way a plain flash stir-fry would.
Stuff into lettuce cups for a lighter next-day lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tastes like a takeout order but comes together in one skillet — and actually holds if a call pulls the crew mid-cook, because the sauce just keeps reducing instead of overcooking the way a flash stir-fry would.
mealPrepNotes: Chop garlic and chilies ahead. This one can simmer a few extra minutes without ruining the dish. Station: Brown the beef hard first, then let the sauce actually simmer and reduce — this is a skillet that can wait on the stove, not a 90-second flash-fry. Station: Add basil off heat at the very end so it stays bright green, not wilted and black. Station: If a call interrupts after the sauce goes in, just cover and hold on low — it won't overcook the way a stir-fry would.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos. Use a certified gluten-free or vegetarian 'oyster' sauce alternative. Use a certified gluten-free broth or bouillon.
